title: PSN Synergy Collector — Live-Disk Inventory Feed for the Inspector
brief: Pure Node.js script that reads the PRISM filesystem and emits a live `PSNLegInventory[]` snapshot for PSNSynergyInspectorEngine. Closes R1 of the inspector envelope: the engine is pure by design, but production callers had no canonical way to produce real inventories — they would have to either inject hand-curated fixtures (defeating the purpose) or each re-derive their own walkers (defeating reuse). This script is the canonical caller-side feeder.

close_out_log.note: scripts/psn-synergy-collect.mjs — ~280 LOC pure Node script reading all 11 PSN legs from disk (obsidian_brain via C:/Users/wompu/.claude/projects/H--prism/memory, prism_os via dispatcher action enum, wiki via knowledge/wiki, memories via knowledge/memories, tribal via knowledge/wiki/code-tribal + tribal-extract, system_viz via state/shared/system-viz/system-graph.json, engines via mcp-server/src/engines, algorithms via mcp-server/src/algorithms, formulas via mcp-server/src/physics, nn_gnn via mcp-server/src/nn-graph, prism_ai via mcp-server/src/engines/PRISM*). Cross-ref scanners use cheap regex on sampled content (CONTENT_SAMPLE_BYTES=16384, FILE_CAP_PER_LEG=5000) — bounded scan so a runaway directory cannot wedge the script. Outputs state/shared/psn-synergy-snapshot.{json,md}: JSON is the machine input for `prism_intelligence:psn_synergy_inspect`, MD is the operator-readable per-leg table. First run: 11 legs, 299,904 nodes counted, runtime <2s.

units.description: The inspector engine is pure by design (R12 fail-loud caller-supplies inventories). This script is the caller — reads disk, builds `PSNLegInventory[]`, writes the snapshot. Operators can now run `node scripts/psn-synergy-collect.mjs && prism_intelligence:psn_synergy_inspect` from any chat and get a real ranked bridge list rather than fixture-only output.

acceptance: scripts/psn-synergy-collect.mjs runs to completion on this repo, writes state/shared/psn-synergy-snapshot.{json,md}, and produces an 11-leg inventory the inspector can rank without further massaging. First run measured 11 legs / 299,904 nodes counted in <2s.

risks.description: Cross-ref scanners are regex-based heuristics on sampled content (first 16KB per file). A wiki entry referencing an engine deep in its body past the sample window will not be counted. Mitigation: the sample size is a knob (CONTENT_SAMPLE_BYTES); raise for finer accuracy at scan-time cost. The ranking is robust to noise — it's the *zero-ref* pairs that matter most, and those are insensitive to sample size.

tribal leg currently scans `knowledge/wiki/code-tribal` + `knowledge/tribal-extract` — the live tribal-tip corpus also has surfaces at `data/tribal-tips/*.json` and inside engines. First-run snapshot shows tribal=0 which surfaces a (likely real but partly synthetic) P0_critical bridge candidate. Follow-up unit P1-U01 (out of scope here) will fold those additional surfaces in.

FILE_CAP_PER_LEG=5000 means very large legs (obsidian_brain, wiki, system_viz already capped) under-count node totals. Cross-ref signals remain meaningful because they're directional — under-wired pairs surface regardless of cap. Mitigation: cap is a knob; raise for one-off precision runs.
